To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed quaternion-based correlation filters, when combined with a quaternionic representation of face image features, improve the performance of the recognition systems in terms of both identification accuracy and computational cost.

the proposed quaternion-based correlation filters can cope with the effects produced by the presence of non-properly illuminating conditions and the use of quaternion-based filters in conjunction with a two-level DWT is the most suitable combination for the task of face recognition.
quaternionic representations of the face image features and correlation filtering in the quaternion domain can be combined to obtain a good illumination-invariant face recognition system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of quaternion correlation filters to improve the performance of face recognition algorithms in the presence of illumination changes.
the development of quaternion-based correlation filters and their application to illumination invariant face recognition.
the design of illumination-invariant face recognition systems that are based on the quaternion representation and the quaternion correlation filters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quaternionic approach is the best choice for the design of correlation filters in face recognition systems.
the use of the STOQF is the best approach to obtain the best results in terms of face recognition accuracy.
the use of the STOQF in combination with the DIF method is the most effective approach to cope with illumination invariance in the face recognition task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of quaternion-based correlation filters is a good alternative to the use of the UOTQF.

the use of the quaternion-based correlation filters, together with a quaternionic representation of face image features, is a good choice for face recognition systems when dealing with non-properly-illuminated face images.
the quaternionic approach is an effective way of dealing with the effects of illumination in face recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a quaternion-based correlation filters can be successfully combined with different face feature extraction methods in order to cope illumination effects in face recognition systems.
the proposed method is able to achieve state-of-the-art results in face recognition, outperforming several other state-of-the-art methods.
the quaternion-based correlation filters outperforms the UOTQF and STOQF in the case of the face recognition experiments.
